title: adp-discovery interview skill
summary: The first adp-discovery skill guides a stakeholder from a product idea to a reviewable discovery baseline. A later Codex session can continue from the saved checklist and decision register. This replay uses the supplied brief as its evidence and leaves workspace handling and acceptance details open.

dimensions.question: What outcome should the product achieve, and for whom?
What work belongs inside the product's scope, and where are its boundaries?
Who uses, approves, or is affected by this product?
What observable result would tell stakeholders that the product works?
What limits, dependencies, or obligations shape the product?
What should trigger the skill, and when should it ask for clarification?
What should the skill produce, and what happens when a needed input is missing?
What must another session or person be able to recover and verify?
Which adjacent skills or workflows share responsibilities or inputs?
Which representative cases should demonstrate success, failure, and recovery?
Who reviews the results, and what evidence is sufficient for acceptance?
Which actions require approval, and who can grant it?
What information may be accessed, retained, or shared, and by whom?

records.text: The brief asks for a complete discovery workflow for an unfamiliar product and recommends discovering the framework itself first.
records.source: Supplied brief, development strategy and first success criterion

records.text: Help the project stakeholder turn a product idea into a reviewable baseline that can be resumed and checked.
The brief describes a Discovery-only first slice built from a reusable catalog and one working interview skill, followed by additional skills.
records.source: Supplied brief, milestones and implementation split

records.text: Focus the first version on the Discovery phase with the interview skill and local workspace files.
Expose the workflow as the repository's interview skill, invokable with $interview.
The brief requires an interrupted interview to continue in a fresh thread without losing confirmed decisions.
Use saved workspace state as the source for resuming a discovery interview.
The first pilot should produce a coherent brief, decision register, open questions, and a preliminary readiness assessment.
Export the brief, confirmed decisions, open questions, and preliminary readiness from saved state.
The brief calls for an independent acceptance check and scenarios involving an incomplete idea, conflicting answers, and interruption.
Check normal discovery, incomplete input, contradiction recovery, and resumption with tests independent of the skill's judgment.
Interview content may contain sensitive stakeholder information. The pilot applies the Security overlay on this assumption.
Which interview content may the team retain and share, and who may access the workspace?
Who can authorize sharing or exporting stakeholder evidence outside the interview workspace?
Who will sign off on the first live interview and which observations will they require?
What overlap will need a clear ownership rule when the companion skills are introduced?
